newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hopes Algeria poll will curb violence.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hopes Algeria poll will curb violence.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it hoped elections in Algeria on Thursday could help end violence in the North African country where tens of thousands have been killed over the past five years.
"These are very important elections occurring tomorrow ... in Algeria," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.

"We hope this election, if credible and if transparent, can mark another step towards national reconciliation and the cessation of violence and the restoration of prosperity in Algeria, and end the terrorism in Algeria."
Burns told reporters Washington would be "watching these elections very closely".

The government of President Liamine Zeroual says the poll is key to resolving the country's civil strife which began when the authorities cancelled general elections in January 1992 which the now outlawed radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) was poised to win.
An estimated 60,000 people have been killed since then.
